question: Does this pipeline's training-and-serving path transmit adaptation at all, when deliberately pushed with a high learning rate and multiple epochs? Closes Limitation 13 of 'A Preregistered Null Result That Did Not Reproduce in a Second Training Environment.'
why_now: Limitation 13 names this run as outstanding. Its marginal evidentiary value is lower than when the limitation was first written -- Table 2's three retrains at the ORIGINAL recipe (lr=5e-6, 1 epoch) already produced +9.61pp (p=2.7e-7), +10.90pp (p=3.4e-8), and +8.77pp (p=1.4e-6) against their same-session nulls -- but the paper still lists it as open, and this machine (RTX 5080) is only available for a limited window, so it is run now rather than left outstanding. [Corrected 2026-08-20: an earlier draft of this field paraphrased the range as '+9.6 to +10.9pp' and the p-values as a blanket 'p<1e-6', both of which mis-stated Table 2 (the low end is +8.77pp, and the third p-value of 1.4e-6 does not satisfy 'p<1e-6'). Fixed to the exact per-retrain numbers before this document was used to justify or interpret anything.]

metric.rationale: Same estimator as prereg_track_a_run1.json -- unbiased pass@k requires n i.i.d. draws; no greedy blend.
metric.secondary: none (intentional deviation from prereg_track_a_run1.json, which also declares pass@3 secondary). This run's decision rule is defined solely on the primary Welch test at a fixed 5pp threshold; a secondary pass@3 estimate would not feed the decision rule and is left out to keep the prereg's committed analysis surface small, not omitted by oversight.

design.sizing_note: Same instrument, same n=40/arm, same test as prereg_track_a_run1.json, so its sizing carries over unchanged: se_diff = 0.0476*sqrt(2/40) = 1.064pp, MDE at 80% power = 2.8*1.064 = 2.98pp. The decision rule's 5pp success threshold sits comfortably above this MDE, so the design is adequately powered to resolve the effect size the decision rule actually requires, not just to detect *some* nonzero effect.
design.test: Welch t-test on run-level pass@1, two-sided, alpha=0.05, each arm retaining its own variance
design.stopping_rule: FIXED N. No peeking, no early stop on effect. Re-size on variance only, exactly as prereg_track_a_run1.json's stopping rule -- if this run's observed sd deviates materially from the assumed 0.0476, that changes the achieved sensitivity, not the fixed N=40 itself.
design.session_discipline: Same-session, interleaved replicate-by-replicate (not sequential blocks), per poscontrol/START-HERE.md rule 4. The null is served FRESH in this session -- not pooled with any prior null from a different session, per rule 1.
design.decision_rule_fixed_in_advance: Success (pipeline transmits adaptation) iff p < 0.05 AND observed effect (positive_control - null) >= +5.00 percentage points. Any other outcome (not significant, or significant but < 5pp, or significant in the negative direction) is reported as-is, not reframed post hoc.

training_recipe.lr_note: ~40x the paper's original 5e-6, which the paper itself notes was an unusually low rate for LoRA (sourced from the alignment-handbook zephyr QLoRA-DPO recipe, not a LoRA-specific default). 2e-4 is a standard-for-LoRA rate, deliberately combined with 3 epochs (vs 1) to make this an unambiguous positive control rather than a fourth ordinary retrain.
training_recipe.seed_note: train_native.py sets no seed (paper Method, 'Initialization Was Not Controlled'). This run inherits that -- it is not fixed here, consistent with every other adapter in this project's record.

verifier_fingerprint.note: Intentional 4-file fingerprint (adds task_bank.py to the 3-file set prereg_track_a_run1.json used) -- this is dataset_gate.verifier_fingerprint()'s actual current output, matches poscontrol/fingerprint_audit.py's real 4-key check, and matches the paper's own 'four-file verifier fingerprint' language. track_a_run1's fingerprint predates the fix that added task_bank.py; this is not a drift from that convention, it's the same live function computed after Failure 4's own repair.

environment.machine: student lab PC, not the original RTX 4080 or the replication's RTX 4090
environment.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080, Blackwell, compute capability sm_120
environment.python: 3.12.10 (not 3.11.9 -- another stack difference from the original run, recorded rather than hidden)
environment.tdr_mitigation_status: NOT APPLIED. This machine is a shared student lab PC with no admin access at run time; HKLM TdrDelay could not be raised from its 2s Windows default, and the wipe-on-logoff policy rules out a scheduled elevated fix within this session. The paper's Discussion states, in its own words, 'We conclude that silent hardware timeouts caused the initial null result' -- but that conclusion rests on a single non-tabulated result (a +10.3pp local replication under the original PEFT 0.14 stack after TDR mitigation, reported only in prose) rather than the same statistical treatment given to Table 2's three retrains. It is the paper's stated conclusion, not its most independently-verified one -- corrected here from an earlier draft of this field that called it the paper's 'root-cause finding', language that overstated its evidentiary weight and is not how the paper's own Limitation 3 treats the broader question of which stack variable matters ('no claim is made that any particular library caused the difference'). Without the registry fix, whatever risk TDR poses is NOT closed for this run regardless of how the paper's claim is weighted. Mitigation used instead: the Windows System event log (Event ID 4101, source Display, plus WHEA-Logger, Kernel-Power id 41, and any nvlddmkm/nvidia provider hit) was checked for a clean baseline (zero hits) before training started, and will be re-checked in the exact training window immediately after training completes and again a few minutes later -- turning 'silent' corruption into 'detected' corruption if it recurs, even though it cannot be prevented at the driver level this session. Any hit in that window is grounds to discard this adapter outright, per the distrust rule recorded alongside the post-training runbook.

what_this_CANNOT_show: Which stack variable (if any) explains the original null vs the retrains' +10pp -- this run adds a fourth combination of variables (new GPU, new driver, new Python, same peft/transformers/trl pins) rather than isolating one. That isolation is Limitation 3's open item, planned as a separate same-session peft-version comparison if time on this machine allows.
Anything about DPO as a general method beyond this one adapter -- single checkpoint, unseeded, exactly as every other adapter in this project's record.

Whether the TDR risk actually fired during THIS run beyond what the before/after event-log check can detect -- the check is real but bounded to what Event ID 4101 logs; a corruption mode that does not trigger a TDR log entry would not be caught by it.
